decks.name: My stories
decks.description: Alex Rivera's stories from the story bank (sample).

cards.q: Tell me about a launch you're proud of.
cards.a:
S: Northwind was adding an analytics add-on and sales had no clear story for it.
T: Own positioning and the launch plan.
A: Ran 25 customer interviews, wrote the positioning, trained sales before launch. Hard part: getting product to drop two features from the message.
R: 1,200 paying accounts in two quarters; Launch of the Year.

cards.q: How do you make sure sales uses what you build?
cards.a:
S: Reps were losing deals to one competitor; old battlecards sat unread.
T: Build something they'd use in calls.
A: Built battlecards with the 40 account executives; updated every quarter from lost-deal notes.
R: Win rate against that competitor went from 31% to 38%.

cards.q: Tell me about a mistake you made.
cards.a:
S: My first pricing page test ran two weeks before I saw tracking only counted one of two demo forms.
T: Save the test and the team's trust.
A: Told my manager the same day, fixed tracking, restarted with a written plan.
R: The rerun lifted demo requests 18%; the plan became the team template.

cards.q: Tell me about a disagreement with another team.
cards.a:
S: Product wanted a feature-list launch; sales wanted a cost-savings story.
T: Land one message both teams would use.
A: Brought customer quotes to a working session; tested both in two email campaigns.
R: Cost-savings won on replies; product agreed; kept a feature appendix.

decks.name: Product marketing technical
decks.description: From the B2B SaaS product marketing field primer (sample).

cards.q: What's the difference between positioning and messaging?
cards.a:
Positioning: who it's for, what it's compared with, and why it wins.
Messaging: the words that bring that positioning to life for each audience.
Example: Northwind Insights positioning from 25 customer interviews.

cards.q: How do you measure whether a launch worked?
cards.a:
Pick the metrics before launch: adoption, pipeline, win rate.
Example: Insights, 1,200 paying accounts in two quarters.

Customers pay for what they use instead of per seat.
A gap for Alex: say so plainly, then the Globex pricing page test and how you'd learn it.
